title: 'The G Engines Are Coming' article arrives on Cook's desk

tellings.quote: there was an article that showed up on my desk. I mean, people would send stuff to us at Jane's.
there's a really interesting article from 1956 called the G engines are coming or something like that.
tellings.difference: Leaves out Cook and credits Gladish, Deser and Arnowitt instead of Trimble.
tellings.link_reason: The same 1956 'The G Engines Are Coming' article as the story where it reaches Cook at Jane's.

plain: This is about an old magazine article from 1956 titled "The G Engines Are Coming", meaning engines that would work by controlling gravity. A journalist named Nick Cook, who worked at Jane's Defence Weekly, a British magazine about military technology, says the article turned up on his desk in 1994. He says readers often sent things to the magazine, and this was one of them. Cook links it to George Trimble, a name the article brings up. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, also mentions the same article on a different show. Michels instead connects it to Michael Gladish, Stanley Deser and Richard Arnowitt, and leaves Cook out. If the article means what they suggest, the aviation world was openly chasing anti-gravity in the 1950s.
